notes.meaning: People can think through their ideas and prepare their plans, but the Lord gives the right words and decides the outcome. A person may weigh many thoughts in mind, yet finding the fitting and effective answer is ultimately a gift from God. This reminds us to depend on the Lord whenever we speak or make decisions.

People naturally believe their own actions are clean and make excuses for their behavior. The Lord looks much deeper, accurately weighing the motives and true condition of the human heart. We need God to examine us because we can easily fool ourselves about our own goodness.

To commit our work to the Lord means to roll the heavy burden of our care onto Him in prayer and faith. When we entrust our duties and future into God's hands, our inner thoughts find peace and our plans succeed. We can live with quiet confidence when we leave the results to Him.

The Lord has formed everything in creation to serve His own purpose and plan. Even people who choose evil do not derail God's world, for they are reserved for the day of judgment. In the end, God's wisdom and justice will be honored in all things.

differ.view: God has sovereignly appointed all things for His own glory, and His justice is glorified even in the appointed destruction of the wicked.
God did not create anyone for the purpose of destruction, but foresees human choices and prepares punishment according to what people deserve.
God does not make anyone wicked, but patiently endures with sinners until the day of judgment falls on those who refuse to repent.
God created human beings with the capacity to choose, and He includes their freely chosen rebellion within His overarching plan without causing evil.

notes.meaning: The Lord detests anyone who is full of self-importance and pride. Even if proud people band together to support one another, they will not escape God's sure judgment. Real safety is found only in humbling ourselves before our Maker.

Sin is atoned for, or covered and forgiven, through faithful love and truth, while reverent fear of the Lord keeps people away from evil. When we experience God's mercy, it breaks the power of sin in our lives. A holy respect for God protects our feet from straying into wrongdoing.

differ.view: Atonement comes solely through God's covenant mercy and truth revealed in Christ, never through human good deeds or charity.
A person's merciful and truthful life serves as a fruit of repentance that prepares the heart to receive God's pardon.
Scripture gives good works an atoning or covering role in a broad sense, seeing them as the necessary evidence of thankful, compassionate love.

other.label: Catholic
other.view: Sins are expiated through human deeds of mercy, kindness, and almsgiving toward one's neighbor.

notes.meaning: When someone's daily life brings pleasure to the Lord, God has the power to bring peace even with former foes. The Lord holds every heart in His hands and can soften or turn away human hostility. Living faithfully before God often disarms our fiercest critics.

Having only a modest income earned honestly is far better than enjoying vast riches gained by cheating others. Dishonest wealth brings guilt, misery, and eventual ruin, while honest poverty leaves the conscience clean. A simple life lived with integrity provides true satisfaction.

A person can carefully map out a life plan, but the Lord is the one who actually guides each step. Human minds cannot foresee the future, yet God's sovereign direction shapes every outcome. We should make our plans with humble trust in His guiding hand.

A king's rulings carry authoritative weight, so he must take great care never to twist justice. Because rulers represent God's authority, their judgments should reflect divine fairness rather than personal whims. Leaders carry a serious duty before God to protect what is right.

Accurate scales and fair weights are appointed by the Lord, who cares about honest dealing in daily commerce. God gave people the wisdom to create standards of trade so that no one would be cheated. Practicing fairness in our daily work honors God, who hates dishonest shortcuts.

Good rulers detest wicked deeds because a government remains stable only when built on justice. Rulers who act fairly earn the loyalty of their people and the protection of God's blessing. Doing what is right provides the greatest security for any leader.

Wise kings appreciate truthful speech and love counselors who speak with honesty. Good leaders prefer straight talk over deceitful flattery that conceals dangerous problems. Speaking the truth with respect is the best way to earn lasting honor.

An earthly ruler's anger can bring swift danger, like a messenger sent to announce execution. A wise person knows how to speak prudently and calm that rage before harm takes place. Using gentle, thoughtful words helps bring peace in dangerous moments.

A ruler's favor brings life and security to those who serve him. His kindness is like a spring rain cloud that waters the fields just before harvest, ensuring a plentiful crop. In an even greater way, knowing God's favor fills our lives with joy and spiritual fruit.

Gaining godly wisdom is far more valuable than gathering heaps of gold and silver. Worldly treasure only provides for our physical needs for a short time, but spiritual understanding enriches the soul forever. Seeking God's truth brings lasting joy that money cannot buy.

The main road of the upright deliberately turns away from sin, keeping travelers safe from harm. Whoever pays close attention to daily conduct guards his life from ruin. Staying on God's path protects us from stumbling into dangerous traps.

Arrogance marches straight toward ruin, and a boastful spirit leads to a painful fall. When people feel superior and self-sufficient, they stop watching for danger and invite God's discipline. We need to watch our own hearts for pride before it brings us down.

It is much better to live with a modest spirit among the poor than to share stolen loot with the arrogant. Humility brings peace with God, even if the world treats humble people with contempt. Choosing a quiet and gentle life preserves our souls from many temptations.

Whoever listens carefully to God's instruction will find good success in life. True happiness, however, comes from personally putting our faith and confidence in the Lord. Walking in obedience and trusting God brings peace in every season.

A person whose heart is filled with wisdom will be recognized as prudent and discerning. Gracious and pleasant speech makes teaching far more appealing and effective to those who listen. Sharing truth with kindness helps others receive it gladly.

Good understanding is like a refreshing spring of water that brings ongoing life and strength to its owner. In contrast, the stubborn foolishness of a fool acts as its own punishment, producing more nonsense. Wise judgment protects our lives from needless disaster.

A wise heart carefully teaches the mouth what to say and adds persuasive power to a person's lips. Words carry real weight when they are backed by thoughtful reflection and genuine truth inside. Developing an understanding heart helps us speak with clear purpose.

Kind and gracious words are as sweet as fresh honey from the comb, bringing comfort to the soul and health to the body. Words of encouragement and biblical truth soothe troubled minds and restore inner strength. Speaking gently can bring deep healing to people who are hurting.

A particular path can look completely right and appealing to a person, yet lead straight to ruin and death. People often deceive themselves by following their feelings rather than God's clear truth. We must test our choices by God's word to avoid deadly traps.

A laborer's natural hunger works on his behalf because the need to eat pushes him to keep working. God designed our daily physical needs to encourage healthy diligence and keep us from laziness. Working faithfully is God's appointed way to provide for our lives.

A troublemaker puts great effort into digging up rumors and slander to ruin someone else's reputation. His speech acts like a scorching fire, spreading damage and hurt wherever his words land. We should refuse to use our tongues to burn down another person's good name.

A deceitful person stirs up constant arguments, and a gossip divides even the closest of friends. Whispering rumors breaks down mutual trust and causes deep heartache between people who once loved each other. Guarding our words preserves our most precious relationships.

A violent person charms his neighbor to lead him into bad situations and down destructive roads. He tries to drag others into his harmful habits and selfish schemes. We must be on guard against companions who urge us toward lawless behavior.

A person who winks slyly or bites his lips is secretly scheming to carry out wickedness. These subtle facial gestures reveal someone whose heart is already set on doing harm. We should be cautious when dealing with people who plot trouble behind hidden signals.

Silver hair is a beautiful crown of honor when it is found in a life of godliness and integrity. Old age deserves natural respect, but it is especially glorious when a person has walked faithfully with God for many years. A righteous life spent in God's service leaves a rich legacy.

Controlling one's own temper is greater than being a mighty soldier, and ruling one's spirit is better than capturing a fortified city. Subduing our own sinful passions requires far more steady discipline and wisdom than winning an outward war. God honors patient self-restraint over physical power.

People may cast lots into the folds of a robe to make a choice, but the Lord determines every single outcome. What looks to human eyes like sheer luck or random chance is entirely guided by God's sovereign hand. We can rest peacefully knowing that nothing in our lives happens outside His care.

differ.view: Casting lots was an Old Testament method of determining God's will that ceased after Pentecost, so the church should no longer practice it.
This verse teaches God's total control over every seemingly random event, and lots may still be used prayerfully to resolve weighty matters that cannot otherwise be decided.
